analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (date bump, and a line ~52 note that inline video accepts constant or variable frame rate) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (date bump, and the GLM5Next request-control table around lines 1147-1153). No executable code, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache or fan-helper behavior changes. The units for cli-reference.md lines 1310-1821 are unchanged context, so I found no security-relevant edit there. The protocol-messages table now documents these behaviors: null reasoning members are treated as unset; reasoning.summary and generate_summary are accepted as no-ops; a top-level thinking object with type and clear_thinking is accepted; reasoning/reasoning_details are rendered into history as reasoning_content; empty-string tool arguments render as {}; strict tools are served without constrained decoding but each auto call is validated against its schema before exposure (ToolConstraintValidation.validate); and forced tool calls, JSON output modes and media remain rejected. These describe provider input-parsing and validation changes whose code is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify them. Items for later review if the code lands: (1) history-injected reasoning_content could place attacker-controlled text into native prompt delimiters. The doc says ambiguous native delimiters are rejected, but it is unclear whether that covers the newly rendered reasoning fields. (2) The new thinking object must keep strict member validation. (3) Variable-frame-rate video decoding widens the media-parsing surface; T-050 (video plaintext temp files) should be rechecked in the code. The relevant boundaries are TB-002 and TB-007, and the relevant threats are T-050 and T-008. I identified no regressions to the threat-model assets, and the threat model needs no update from these doc edits alone. The code for the described behavior was not supplied, so confidence in those descriptions is limited.
